scene_001.title: Getting Ready
scene_001.narration: You stand in front of your bathroom mirror. On the shelf behind you are your standard toiletries and the stuff you usually take to start your day. You start to grab it out of habit. You stop and think to yourself, 'It's August 1st, Mom's birthday. Just don't use today before dinner. One day, you can do that, can't you?'

scene_002a.title: Mom's Birthday Dinner
scene_002a.narration: You've made it to your mother's birthday dinner. At the dinner table, your siblings talk about their jobs, kids, and the state of the world. Everyone is laughing and enjoying themselves. You're just trying to focus, but it's hard when you didn't get your fix this morning. As your legs bounce under the table and your skin starts to feel too tight for your body, your mom asks, 'You okay honey, you've been quiet tonight?' Everyone looks at you for an answer.

choices.label: You force a smile, 'Just tired. Long week.'

You turn on the lights but it doesn't help much. The weight of your guilt has settled on you too much.

scene_002bB.title: Alone at Home
scene_002bB.narration: You drop yourself onto your bed and reflect on your evening. Do you use to cope with your mental problems, or are your problems from using? You start to imagine what it feels like to fit in, feel like you belong with everyone. The thoughts hit you harder than you expect. You don't have much faith in yourself. You've tried to quit before, and you've always gone back; however, if your problems are a result of your use, it's worth one more shot.

choices.label: Maybe I don't need to quit, just cut back. I can set rules in my head: only on the weekends, or after a bad day at work.

scene_002c.title: Alone at Home

You drop yourself onto your bed, replaying the moments from dinner and the little comforts your family gave you, even if they didn't know the issues were from what you were using. You imagine what it would be like to come to them and tell them, 'I've struggled with using for the past 10 years, but now I'm finally clean.' The thought of it hits you harder than you expect. You don't have much faith in yourself. You've tried to quit before, and you've always gone back; however, for the first time in a long time, trying doesn't feel completely pointless.

scene_003.title: A New Beginning
scene_003.narration: You wake up to a strip of light shining onto your face. For a moment, you just lie there, waiting for your brain to catch up. Your revelation the night before wasn't just a late-night feeling; maybe it really is worth a shot. The thought of quitting makes you uneasy, but you also can't shake off the other side of it. The possibility that everything can finally be different. Are you really ready to fully commit to quitting?

choices.label: Yes, I am ready.

Maybe it is just another workday, but this time you're trying without the one thing that's always held you up.

scene_win.title: One Year Clean
scene_win.narration: For a second, nobody says anything. Your dad blinks hard and looks away. Your mom's eyes fill instantly; she covers her mouth with her hand. One of them reaches for you first, maybe your mom, pulling you into a hug. 'We knew something was up; we just didn't know how bad. I'm so proud of you.' Your dad clears his throat. 'Took a lot of guts to admit that. I'm glad you're here, son.' You start to realize there was never anything you had to worry about; they don't think any differently of you. You've made it a whole year.

scene_relapse.title: A Setback
scene_relapse.narration: This is not the end of the journey, but a warning sign that the urge is stronger than you have been willing to admit. Recovery is not a single perfect moment; it is a series of decisions and the willingness to choose support again.
